arabic_blocks: [946] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن نافع وعبد الله بن دينار عن ابن عمر أن رجلا سأل رسول الله ﷺ عن صلاة الليل، فقال رسول الله عليه السلام صلاة الليل مثنى مثنى فإذا خشي أحدكم الصبح صلى ركعة واحدة توتر له ما قد صلى وعن نافع أن عبد الله بن عمر كان يسلم بين الركعة والركعتين في الوتر حتى يأمر ببعض حاجته
english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘ and ‘Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn ‘Umar:

A man asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about the night prayer. The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said, “The night prayer is two units at a time. If one of you fears the coming of morning, he prays one unit, making what he has prayed odd in number.”
And from Nafi‘:
‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar used to give the closing greeting between the single unit and the two units of Witr, even giving instructions about some need of his.
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: Both complete portions of the selected report are retained, including the second Nafi‘ route and Ibn ‘Umar’s intervening instructions. Dar Ibn Kathir prints them separately as 990 and 991; the single selected reference 946 remains intact. No occurrence has been removed or a new app number invented.

The source has ﷺ in the question and the shorter عليه السلام in the answer. Their English forms remain distinct. Brill uses Prophet in the first designation and the longer honorific in the answer; the selected source is unchanged.
The single-unit/two-unit order in بين الركعة والركعتين is retained. Neither an obligatory classification nor an extra timing instruction is supplied.

arabic_blocks: [947] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن مخرمة بن سليمان عن كريب ان ابن عباس أخبره أنه بات عند ميمونة وهي خالته فاضطجعت في عرض وسادة واضطجع رسول الله ﷺ وأهله في طولها فنام حتى انتصف الليل أو قريبا منه فاستيقظ يمسح النوم عن وجهه ثم قرأ عشر آيات من آل عمران ثم قام رسول الله ﷺ إلى شن معلقة فتوضأ فأحسن الوضوء ثم قام يصلي فصنعت مثله فقمت إلى جنبه فوضع يده اليمنى على رأسي وأخذ بأذني يفتلها ثم صلى ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم أوتر ثم اضطجع حتى جاءه المؤذن فقام فصلى ركعتين ثم خرج فصلى الصبح
english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, that Ibn ‘Abbas informed him:

He spent the night with Maymunah, who was his maternal aunt. I lay across the width of a pillow, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his wife lay along its length. He slept until midnight, or close to it. Then he awoke, wiping sleep from his face, and recited ten verses from Al ‘Imran. Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went to an old waterskin that was hanging and performed ablution well. Then he stood to pray. I did as he had done and stood beside him. He placed his right hand on my head and took hold of my ear, twisting it. Then he prayed two units, then two units, then two units, then two units, then two units, then two units. Then he prayed Witr. Then he lay down until the caller to prayer came to him. He got up and prayed two units, then went out and prayed the morning prayer.
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: All six repeated pairs before Witr are retained individually, as in both inspected Arabic prints. The pinned Khan-family comparison 2.16.106 says five times; that count is not substituted into the translation. Its editorial cross-reference is not part of the selected narration.

The source changes from third-person introduction to first-person account; both are retained. Pillow follows وسادة; bed in the Bewley comparison does not replace it. The source says ten verses, without supplying last.

Both source honorifics, midnight uncertainty, the worn hanging waterskin, right hand, ear-twisting, both later pairs of units and final morning prayer remain. Brill expands Malik to Malik ibn Anas and uses a definite form of pillow; neither change is imported.

arabic_blocks: [948] حدثنا يحيى بن سليمان قال: حدثني ابن وهب قال: أخبرني عمرو أن عبد الرحمن بن القاسم حدثه عن أبيه عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: قال النبي ﷺ صلاة الليل مثنى مثنى فإذا أردت أن تنصرف فاركع ركعة توتر لك ما صليت قال القاسم ورأينا أناسا منذ أدركنا يوترون بثلاث وإن كلا لواسع أرجو أن لا يكون بشيء منه بأس
english_blocks: Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to me. He said: ‘Amr informed me that ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim related to him, from his father, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar. He said:
The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “The night prayer is two units at a time. When you wish to finish, pray one unit, making what you have prayed odd in number.”
Al-Qasim said: Since we reached maturity, we have seen people praying Witr with three units. There is latitude in either way. I hope there is nothing wrong with any of it.

english_blocks: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, that ‘A’ishah informed him:
The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray eleven units. That was his prayer.
She means at night.

In that prayer, he would remain in a prostration for as long as it takes one of you to recite fifty verses before raising his head. He would pray two units before the dawn prayer, then lie on his right side until the caller to prayer came to him for the prayer.

english_blocks: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us. He said: Anas ibn Sirin related to us. He said:

I said to Ibn ‘Umar, “Tell me about the two units before the morning prayer: should I prolong the recitation in them?” He said, “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray at night two units at a time and pray Witr with one unit. He would pray the two units before the morning prayer as though the call to prayer were in his ears.”
Hammad said: Meaning, quickly.

arabic_blocks: [954] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثني مالك عن أبي بكر ابن عمر بن عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن عمر بن الخطاب عن سعيد بن يسار أنه قال: كنت أسير مع عبد الله بن عمر بطريق مكة، فقال سعيد فلما خشيت الصبح نزلت فأوترت ثم لحقته، فقال عبد الله بن عمر أين كنت فقلت: خشيت الصبح فنزلت فأوترت، فقال عبد الله أليس لك في رسول الله ﷺ أسوة حسنة فقلت: بلى والله قال: فإن رسول الله ﷺ كان يوتر على البعير
english_blocks: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Abu Bakr ibn ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, from Sa‘id ibn Yasar, that he said:

I was travelling with ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar on the road to Makkah. Sa‘id said: When I feared the coming of morning, I dismounted and prayed Witr, then caught up with him. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said, “Where were you?” I said, “I feared the coming of morning, so I dismounted and prayed Witr.” ‘Abdullah said, “Do you not have a good example in the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” I said, “Yes, by Allah.” He said, “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray Witr on the camel.”
